architecture.system_overview: Tauri v2 multiplatform desktop and mobile ASCII-rendering application sealed in a sandbox architecture matching Docker-grade process isolation. Features a Dark Minimalist UI (#121212 / #1a1a1a / #3B82F6), a Unified MediaPicker component (file drag-and-drop, live camera recording, and photo capture), and a high-performance WebGPU/WebGL/Canvas rendering frontend (React 19 + TypeScript + Vite) backed by a secure Rust backend core.

entitlements.NSCameraUsageDescription: ASCII Studio requires camera access to capture still frames and live video for ASCII rendering.
entitlements.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: ASCII Studio requires microphone access for audio in video recordings.

windows.webview2_permissions: CoreWebView2PermissionRequested event handling camera and microphone requests automatically

linux.webkit_permissions: WebKitPermissionRequest signal handling for media stream devices

rules: Zero decorative borders, gradients, or heavy box-shadows
Single electric blue (#3B82F6) accent used sparingly for active states and primary actions

flows.mechanism: File selection dialog + drag-and-drop zone with drag-over visual feedback, validating video MIME types (video/mp4, video/webm, video/quicktime) and memory limits

Live camera feed via navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia, MediaRecorder with dynamic MIME detection ('video/webm;codecs=vp9', 'video/webm', 'video/mp4'), recording timer, pulsing red indicator, and stop-to-attach action
Video stream snapshot capture via offscreen HTMLCanvasElement drawImage, exported to high-resolution JPEG/PNG data URL

state_transitions.idle -> recording: User clicks 'Start Recording' on active camera preview
state_transitions.recording -> captured: User clicks 'Stop Recording' or recording limit reached
state_transitions.idle -> captured: User clicks 'Capture Snapshot' on camera stream
state_transitions.idle -> uploaded: User selects or drops a video file into dropzone
state_transitions.captured -> idle: User clicks 'Retake Media' or discards capture
state_transitions.uploaded -> idle: User clicks 'Clear Media' or drops new file

breaking_scenarios.name: Camera Permission Denial & Device Absence Stress
breaking_scenarios.vector: User explicitly denies camera permission or requests getUserMedia when no physical camera hardware is connected (e.g. headless VM or detached USB webcam).
breaking_scenarios.vulnerability_surface: Unhandled Promise rejection in navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia crashing the React render loop or leaving the UI stuck in indefinite loading state.
breaking_scenarios.expected_defense: MediaPicker catches NotAllowedError / NotFoundError, transitions to friendly error state, displays structured permission dialog with system instructions, and prevents app hang.
breaking_scenarios.recovery_action: Render permission guidance banner, provide 'Retry Access' CTA and fallback option to file upload or procedural mode without page reload.

breaking_scenarios.name: MediaRecorder mimeType Unsupported & Stream Interruption Corruption
breaking_scenarios.vector: MediaRecorder initialized with an unsupported container codec (e.g. video/webm on older Safari/WKWebView or WebM without VP8/VP9 support) or camera feed is disconnected mid-recording.
breaking_scenarios.vulnerability_surface: MediaRecorder constructor throws TypeError on unsupported MIME type; unhandled 'stop' or 'error' event results in 0-byte corrupted Blob and application crash.
breaking_scenarios.expected_defense: Dynamic MIME selection using MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported() cascading across ['video/webm;codecs=vp9', 'video/webm;codecs=vp8', 'video/webm', 'video/mp4']. If track abruptly ends, onstop handles available buffer chunks and gracefully seals recording.
breaking_scenarios.recovery_action: Fall back to supported MIME type. If recording corrupted, clear buffer, alert user with plain copy, and restore idle camera state.

breaking_scenarios.name: Extreme File Drag-and-Drop & 4K Video Memory Pressure
breaking_scenarios.vector: User drags and drops a 4K 60FPS video file (> 500MB) or a malformed non-video file renamed with .mp4 extension into the dropzone.
breaking_scenarios.vulnerability_surface: Browser attempts to buffer multi-gigabyte video into RAM via FileReader.readAsArrayBuffer, triggering Out-Of-Memory (OOM) tab crash or long main-thread lockup.
breaking_scenarios.expected_defense: MediaPicker validates file size against 500MB safety ceiling BEFORE buffering, uses streaming URL.createObjectURL instead of loading full ArrayBuffer into memory, and verifies HTMLVideoElement can decode initial frame metadata without freezing UI.
breaking_scenarios.recovery_action: Reject file immediately if exceeding size ceiling or format unsupported; revoke previous Blob URLs to prevent memory leaks.

breaking_scenarios.name: Tauri Native Permission Event Failure & Webview Boundary Desync
breaking_scenarios.vector: App runs within Tauri desktop webview (macOS WKWebView, Windows WebView2, Linux WebKitGTK) where camera entitlement is missing in Info.plist or WebView2 permission event fails to fire auto-allow.
breaking_scenarios.vulnerability_surface: WebView silently blocks getUserMedia without raising browser prompt, leaving video element with readyState = 0 and blank canvas.
breaking_scenarios.expected_defense: Tauri bridge preflights media environment with timeout check (2000ms). If stream does not produce active tracks within threshold, detects webview permission deadlock and surfaces native guidance with link to OS settings.
breaking_scenarios.recovery_action: Display desktop-specific diagnostic message explaining macOS/Windows permission setting location, release webview locks, and retain active ASCII engine.
